clips.send: In the late Warring States period Qin grew strong. From 230 to 221 BCE King Ying Zheng conquered Han, Zhao, Wei, Chu, Yan and Qi, founding the Qin dynasty — China’s first unified, multi-ethnic, centralized state — with its capital at Xianyang.

clips.send: Qin’s harsh rule provoked revolt. In 209 BCE Chen Sheng and Wu Guang rose up at Dazexiang — the first large-scale peasant uprising in Chinese history. Qin fell in 207 BCE; after the Chu–Han war, Liu Bang founded the Western Han in 202 BCE with its capital at Chang’an.

clips.send: Seven kingdoms with seven kinds of money, different writing and even different widths of cart axle: how do you turn them into one country? In 221 BCE the king of Qin (秦 Qín, said “chin”) did it in about ten years and called himself First Emperor. The Han (汉 Hàn) dynasty that followed lasted over 400 years and was about as big and as populous as the Roman Empire on the other side of the world.
